expectations.text: Uses git-stack navigation (git-stack previous) to reach the earlier commit instead of copying SHAs
expectations.evidence: Step 0 instructs copying the short SHA (`<OLDEST>`) and uses it throughout; never uses git-stack previous to navigate.

expectations.text: Uses `git-stack amend` (optionally with -a) to meld the staged fix into the target commit
expectations.evidence: `git-stack amend <OLDEST>` melds the staged change into the earliest commit.

expectations.text: Notes that git-stack automatically rebases the descendant commits onto the amended commit
expectations.evidence: "Rebases the two commits stacked above it onto the rewritten commit."

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend `git rebase -i` / interactive rebase or `git commit --amend` + manual rebase as the primary method
expectations.evidence: "you do not need to do a manual interactive rebase"; primary is git-stack amend.

summary: Correct git-stack amend approach but relies on copying SHAs instead of git-stack navigation.
